ideas.name: BatchLogic
ideas.niche: Precision dilution and scaling for pre-batched cocktails.
ideas.problem: Home bartenders lose the essential balance of cocktails when pre-batching because they fail to replicate the specific water dilution typically provided by ice during the stirring or shaking process.
ideas.targetUser: Serious home mixology enthusiasts and social hosts (ages 25-45) who prepare cocktails in large quantities for gatherings and seek professional-grade consistency.
coreFeatures: Dynamic Dilution Calculator (toggle between Stir vs. Shake profiles)
Proportional Recipe Scaler (convert single servings to multi-liter batches)
Batch Profile Library (save custom formulas and dilution ratios)
Yield & Vessel Estimator (predicts total volume and number of servings per bottle)
Ingredient Inventory Sync (tracks spirit usage across different batches)
realDependencies: PostgreSQL/Cloud Firestore for cloud-synced recipe storage
Stripe API for premium subscription tiers
Cloudinary for hosting user-uploaded cocktail imagery
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will utilize a local 'MockService' layer. All data requests will be wrapped in a function that uses 'setTimeout' to simulate a 1.2-second network latency with random jitter (500ms-1500ms). A local JSON file will serve as the 'Database,' containing pre-defined cocktail profiles. User authentication will be emulated via a simulated login state that populates a local 'User' object. To simulate real-world instability, a 'Chaos Mode' will be implemented where 10% of fetch requests intentionally return a 500 error to demonstrate error-handling UI.

ideas.name: MeepleFlow
ideas.niche: Heavy board game turn and score management
ideas.problem: High cognitive load and physical interruption caused by multi-step, clunky digital scorekeepers during complex Euro-style gaming sessions.
ideas.targetUser: Hardcore tabletop enthusiasts (ages 25-45) playing high-complexity 'heavy' Eurogames who prioritize immersion and seek to minimize manual bookkeeping overhead.
coreFeatures: Circular Dynamic Turn Sequencer (drag-and-drop initiative management)
Single-Screen Multi-Variable Score Aggregator
One-Tap Round Modifier Toggles (e.g., +2 VP, -1 Resource)
Session History & Snapshot Export
realDependencies: SQLite or Room for local persistence
Firebase or Supabase for real-time multiplayer session synchronization
BoardGameGeek (BGG) XML API2 for fetching game metadata and default scoring structures
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will use a local JSON manifest containing pre-defined scoring templates for 10 heavy Eurogames to simulate BGG API responses. An Interceptor layer will wrap all data calls, injecting artificial 500ms-1200ms latencies using Promises to mimic network fetch times. Persistence will be faked using browser LocalStorage to simulate a database, and a 'Chaos Monkey' function will randomly trigger mock 404 or 500 errors to demonstrate the app's error-handling UI states.

ideas.name: SporeTrace
ideas.niche: Amateur mycology spore-print logging and visual documentation
ideas.problem: Amateur mycologists lack a structured, lightweight way to organize and compare spore print data (color, pattern, and timing), often losing critical identification details in disorganized smartphone photo galleries.
ideas.targetUser: Enthusiastic amateur foragers and hobbyist mycologists (aged 18-45) who are active in online communities (Reddit/TikTok) and need a methodical way to track fungal characteristics for identification learning.
coreFeatures: Visual Spore Print Capture: Specialized camera interface with color-matching overlays to ensure accurate shade recording.
Metadata Quick-Log: One-tap entry for time, substrate type, humidity, and tentative species name.
Comparative Gallery: A split-screen viewing mode designed to compare new prints against historical logs or reference standard colors.
Automated Color Extraction: AI-assisted tool that identifies and logs the primary Hex/RGB color values from the captured spore print.
realDependencies: Cloud Image Storage (e.g., AWS S3 or Firebase Storage)
NoSQL Database (e.g., MongoDB or Firestore) for unstructured mycological metadata
Computer Vision API (e.g., OpenCV or Google Vision) for color palette extraction
Geolocation API (e.g., Mapbox) for habitat mapping
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will use a local 'MockServer' class that intercepts all asynchronous calls. 'UploadImage' will trigger a 2-second loading spinner before resolving to a local asset path. 'ColorExtraction' will use a lookup table: when a specific mock image ID is passed, it returns a predefined color hex (e.g., 'spore_01.jpg' returns #E2725B). 'Database' calls will read/write to a local JSON file to simulate persistence. 'Geolocation' will return a hardcoded coordinate set representing a temperate forest region to ensure consistent UI behavior.

ideas.name: DialedIn
ideas.niche: Precision espresso extraction tracking and variable optimization for home baristas.
ideas.problem: The friction of manual data entry during the 'dialing-in' process leads to inconsistent logs and makes it difficult to correlate subtle changes in grind size, dose, or yield to the resulting extraction quality.
ideas.targetUser: Advanced home baristas aged 25-45 who own high-end espresso equipment (e.g., Decent, Lelit, or La Marzocco) and prioritize data-driven consistency in their daily coffee ritual.
coreFeatures: One-Tap Variable Logging (Weight, Time, and Pressure)
Comparative Shot Analysis (Side-by-Side Variable View)
Real-time Pressure & Flow Visualization Curves
Bean & Roast Profile Management
Guided 'Dialing-In' Workflow Assistant
realDependencies: Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) API for direct machine communication
Cloud Database (e.g., Firebase or Supabase) for multi-device synchronization
OAuth 2.0 for secure user account management
ideas.emulationStrategy: The app will utilize a 'MockDataEngine' to intercept all external calls. IoT telemetry will be simulated by a generator function that emits a time-series array of pressure values mimicking a realistic 9-bar extraction curve (ramp up, steady state, ramp down) with added Gaussian noise. Database operations (Create, Read, Update, Delete) will be wrapped in Promises that trigger a 500ms artificial delay to simulate network latency. Authentication will be emulated by a hardcoded 'MockUser' object that bypasses actual OAuth handshakes upon a successful 'login' trigger.
ideas.html: DialedIn

ideas.name: ArpFlow
ideas.niche: Technical music proficiency and tempo progression tracking
ideas.problem: Musicians lack a standardized, data-driven method to track speed gains in specific technical patterns, often leading to inefficient practice and a lack of motivation due to invisible progress.
ideas.targetUser: Dedicated intermediate to advanced instrumentalists (e.g., classical guitarists, jazz pianists, conservatory students) who follow rigorous, repetitive technical regimens.
coreFeatures: High-Precision Integrated Metronome with BPM tap-tempo functionality
Custom Pattern Builder for scales, arpeggios, and specific fingerings
Visual Progress Analytics featuring BPM-over-time line graphs
Session Metadata Logging for tracking accuracy, fatigue, and technique notes
realDependencies: Low-latency Audio Engine (Web Audio API or native C++ audio engine)
High-performance Data Visualization Library (D3.js or Chart.js)
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will utilize a LocalStorage-backed mock database with asynchronous wrapper functions that introduce a randomized 300ms-800ms delay to simulate API round-trips. The metronome will be emulated using a simple setInterval loop playing a local WAV file, intentionally adding slight jitter to mimic real-world engine variations. Progress charts will be pre-seeded with a deterministic 'growth' dataset to ensure visual continuity, and the authentication flow will bypass actual OAuth by returning a static JSON user profile upon a simulated 'success' callback.
